A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, objectives, and certification framework. All 29 pages of each version, including Appendices A–I, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original certification experiments on real and synthetic graphs, including architectural analyses, dynamic graphs, and multiclass results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds an exact-versus-incomplete multiclass comparison on Citeseer in Table 2.

M1.justification: Appendix A.1 refines the existing exact multiclass solver by replacing integer-label and auxiliary big-M constraints with direct one-hot label and flip-budget constraints. The stated formulation shrinks from m integer plus 4Km + 2m + K - 1 binary variables to 3Km + K - 1 binary variables. The binary, collective, and pre-existing incomplete certification procedures remain.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same real and synthetic graph datasets, binary and multiclass node-classification tasks, and dynamic-graph scenarios. The added Citeseer comparison does not expand data or task coverage.

E2.justification: V1 reports exact certification on Citeseer and incomplete certification on Cora-ML separately. V2 additionally evaluates the incomplete certificate against the exact certificate on Citeseer for GCN, SGC, GCN Skip-α, and GCN Skip-PC in Table 2. Other comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: Figure 5b changes the reported adjacency-weight sweep from β = {1, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25, 0} to {1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.1, 0}. Appendix G.2 still lists the earlier 0.75A configuration without supplying the new 0.1A hyperparameter. Other stated splits, metrics, and cross-validation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 and Table 2 add a direct test of how closely incomplete multiclass certification matches exact certification on Citeseer. Figure 5b revises the graph-weight sensitivity study; the other architectural, connectivity, size, and dynamic-graph analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five seeds, three for multiclass datasets, and report standard deviations. The new table follows this existing practice; changed error-bar values do not establish a change in statistical methodology.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds incomplete Citeseer results, including SGC certified accuracy of 34.7% versus 35.3% exact at epsilon = 0.01. Figure 16a revises existing exact results: SGC at epsilon = 0.02 changes from approximately 7.3% to 9.3%. Figure 5b replaces an ablation curve. V2 also has a discrepancy: Table 2 reports 20.3% for GCN Skip-PC at epsilon = 0.01, while Figure 16a plots approximately 21.3%.

T1.justification: Appendix A substantially revises the multiclass derivation, using prediction uniqueness to remove an optimization level, combining classwise dual problems, and deriving new adversary constraints. The maximum-selector constraint now correctly excludes the originally predicted class. However, the newly displayed joint objective in Equation 22 has a negative quadratic term, inconsistent with Equation 2 and the subsequent KKT formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal claims about exact certification, robustness hierarchies, and plateauing remain. The conclusion adds the substantive claim that the incomplete multiclass certificate often matches exact certification while offering better scalability; v1 merely pointed to the existing relaxation as a scalability strategy.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a hypothesis explaining near-tightness through flips from the predicted class to the runner-up class. It also identifies larger regularization constants as an obstacle to exact Cora-ML certification. Existing finite-width and plateau-mechanism limitations remain.

D1.justification: Code-access instructions change from Figshare with a release-upon-acceptance statement to GitHub instructions in the abstract and reproducibility statement. Appendix A.2 newly reports incomplete Cora-ML certification taking about 20 minutes per node on two CPUs, with rare cases reaching six hours. This is additional disclosure, not evidence of a changed computing allocation.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior poisoning certificates remain unchanged. The comparison with Gosch et al. and attribution of the incomplete multiclass strategy were already present in v1.

P1.justification: Appendix A separates exact and inexact certification into subsections, moves the existing relaxation discussion, and rewrites the derivation narrative. Elsewhere, changes consist mainly of localized prose compression, an expanded scalability paragraph, and conference-header edits.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 2 and renumbers subsequent tables. Figures 1, 3, and 5 are relocated, several plots adjust horizontal spacing or legend placement, and Figure 5b changes legend entries. The overall visual organization and existing figure inventory are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the multiclass extension through a simpler formulation, correction of the maximum-selector constraint, and a direct tightness comparison absent from v1. Runtime and code-access disclosures also help reproducibility. These provide a limited net gain, tempered by the new Equation 22 sign error and inconsistencies between revised plots and their accompanying table or hyperparameter details.
